cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Outdo the Effort
cards.instruction: Answer every favor, chore, or sacrifice with a bigger one that restores your lead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Thanks for the lift. I'll cover your Saturday shift.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No need. I covered yours yesterday so you could rest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then I'll take your whole weekend. You shouldn't be doing more than me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already swapped Sunday to drive you to the airport.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll cancel my flight and cover your holiday. You deserve the longer break.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 assert decision authority, but A5 ordinary offer to cancel travel does not sustain permission over the other person relief.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 prior cover causes A3 weekend offer; B4 Sunday driving sacrifice causes A5 canceled flight and holiday cover, after unrelated restriction.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 reveal actual helpful sacrifices, plausibly trying to spare A while A insists on doing more.

heightening.evidence: B4 sacrifice made for A trip leads A5 to cancel that trip and offer a longer break in return.

specificity.evidence: A1 lift and shifts, B2 prior rest cover and B4 airport drive establish concrete favors in time and effort.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 canceling the trip B rearranged for is earned by B4 favor, although the A3 stock command is intrusive.
